Morning, George — Tuesday, the fourth of August.

Two big threads today.

That heat's still parked over Athens, another scorcher with the fire risk staying high, so keep it in mind if you head out west.

And the Iran story took a sharp turn — Trump's now calling this Tehran's last chance to sign a deal, even as Iran quietly digs in.

— personal items —

Abroad, it's still all about Iran.

After Trump called off that weekend strike and talks got going, he's turned the rhetoric right up — calling these negotiations Iran's last chance for a decent deal, and warning darkly of decapitation if they walk.

Trouble is, Tehran's pushing back: its foreign ministry says the Oman talks are strictly about who runs the Strait of Hormuz, not some broader peace with Washington.

So Trump's talking up an imminent agreement while Iran signals it's agreed to no such thing.

Nothing's signed, and the gap between the two sides looks wider today than it did yesterday.

And from the science desk, a good one for you as an athlete.

Researchers at Rockefeller found that arginine — an amino acid you get from meat, nuts, and seeds — is basically the fuel your immune system needs to spot cancer and viruses.

Starve cells of it and tumours and infections slip by unnoticed; feed mice a high-arginine diet and it crushed colon tumours and blunted both flu and COVID.

It's early, and it's mice, but a neat reminder of how much what you eat steers your defences.

Over to AI, and the frontier's gone quiet again — no new ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or Grok worth the name in the last day, and Claude Opus 5 from a couple of weeks back is still top of the rankings.

But here's the shift actually worth your attention as an app builder: the real action's moved to cheap open-weight coding models — the likes of Kimi, DeepSeek, and GLM — which are getting good enough at writing code to rival the paid tiers for a fraction of the cost.

— personal items —

Google's proper flagship Gemini, meanwhile, still hasn't actually shipped, so treat any launch buzz as rumour.

Weather at home: more of the same furnace.

Mid-twenties first thing, up to around thirty-three by mid-afternoon under clear skies, then easing back to the high twenties in the evening.

No rain to speak of, a gusty northerly Meltemi wind — which is exactly what's been feeding the fires — and with the ground bone-dry, the danger stays high.

Sun sets just after half past eight.

Speaking of which, that big wildfire west of Athens is still burning.

Water-bombers and helicopters were back up at first light, a day after the deadly mid-air collision, with more than a thousand people already evacuated.

Investigators reckon it started from a faulty power line off a private wind-turbine site.

On the markets, oil took a proper tumble — Brent fell about five percent to below eighty dollars a barrel, unwinding all that war-risk premium now that Trump's paused the strikes and both sides are at least talking.

Good news at the pump, if nothing else.

And a quick one for the backlog: the two Epic freebies, OTXO and Sol Cesto, are only free to keep through Wednesday, so grab them today if you want them.

After that it swaps to Beacon Pines and a co-op puzzler, We Were Here Together.

Onto your world.

The written briefing

World

  • Iran — Trump ramps up as talks stall. After calling off a weekend strike at Gulf allies’ request, Trump escalated the rhetoric, branding the negotiations Iran’s “last chance” for a decent deal and warning of “decapitation.” But Tehran pushed back: its foreign ministry insists the Oman talks are only about who administers the Strait of Hormuz, not a broader peace with Washington. Nothing is signed and the two sides look further apart today. Washington Times · CNN
  • Science — an amino acid that sharpens immunity. Rockefeller researchers report (Jul 30, Cell) that arginine — found in meat, nuts and seeds — is needed to translate MHC-I, the protein that flags cancer and viral material to T-cells. Starved of it, tumours and infections evade detection; a high-arginine diet quashed colon tumours and blunted flu and COVID in mice. Early and animal-only, but a striking diet–immunity link. ScienceDaily · Science News · Cell
